clue.text: Peculiar personal impressions

blocks.note: surface reading: odd private opinions someone has formed
setter's reading: marks pressed onto a surface that are unique to each individual

explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressions' looks like opinions and 'peculiar' like strange, but here peculiar means belonging to one person only, and the impressions are physical marks left by the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Every person leaves inked or smudged ridge patterns from their own hand, which police use to identify them.

clue.text: Chance including equipment for a certain craft

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: fate is fortune or chance
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: A gamble involving the right gear for a particular skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a skill; it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship, so it is one particular vessel or boat.

clue.text: Some fine palaeolithic tools can be seen here

definitions.text: Some fine palaeolithic tools can be seen here

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters are a part of the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling these two words

explanation.surface: A museum guide notes where Stone Age implements may be viewed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: stone tools have been found in the Himalayan country.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone Age implements have been found in the Himalayan kingdom, so it is a place one might view them.

clue.text: Convertible put nearer entrance

indicators.note: something convertible can be changed into another form, so the letters are re-formed

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An open-topped car is parked closer to the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' reads as a doorway; it is the verb meaning to put in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to delight and captivate them, which is to fill them with rapture.

clue.text: Parking place for sport

blocks.note: P is the road-sign letter for parking
to lay something down is to place it

explanation.surface: A car park is set aside for games.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport and play both mean amusement or fun; to sport is to frolic.

clue.text: Meant to get betrothed

blocks.note: first meaning: planned or done on purpose
second meaning: a fiance or fiancee, the person one is engaged to

explanation.surface: Someone was destined to become engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past participle of a verb for planning, and also a noun for one's future spouse.

clue.text: The royal family possibly tour round hundreds

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered
round means surrounding, so the reordered letters go about the other piece

blocks.note: the letters of tour, reordered
D is the Roman numeral 500, five hundreds

explanation.surface: The monarchy perhaps goes on a tour among hundreds of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English dynasty of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I, a royal house.

clue.text: Left at six with an overbearing set of people

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
VI is six in Roman numerals
read as an over bearing: in a down clue an sits above S, south, a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned at six o'clock with a domineering group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overbearing' looks like one word meaning bossy; split it, and an sits over a bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvians are the nationals of a Baltic state, a group or nation of people.

clue.text: He robs a mite and gets put inside

indicators.note: something put inside is placed within another thing, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: a mite is a tiny amount, a bit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A petty thief steals a small sum and is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put inside' suggests prison, fitting the robber, but it places one word in another.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an outlaw who robs travellers, so he is a robber.

clue.text: Bring in a social worker-it's vital

blocks.note: to import goods is to bring them in from abroad
the ant is a social insect, and its sterile females are called workers

explanation.surface: Recruiting a social worker is described as essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare professional, but it is an insect from a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is of great consequence or essential, the same sense as significant or crucial.

clue.text: Work force housed by an American lawyer

indicators.note: something housed by another is lodged inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney, a public prosecutor in the US
to ram something is to force it in or through

explanation.surface: A US attorney is put in charge of a labour force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like labour but is a piece of writing for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a literary work, and a drama is a play written for performance.

clue.text: A Pole's somewhat odd leaning

indicators.note: something odd is out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their usual order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A Polish person has rather eccentric tendencies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaning' reads as an inclination of the Pole, but it means tilted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aslope is set at a slant, sloping or tilted rather than upright.

clue.text: Deeply impressed, and serious in consequence

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, so one piece is surrounded

blocks.note: an end is an outcome or result
a grave matter is a serious one

explanation.surface: Someone was profoundly moved and solemn as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deeply impressed' seems to describe a feeling, but it means cut into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters engraved on metal or stone are cut deeply into it, literally pressed in.

clue.text: Well-documented racial issue

blocks.note: surface reading: a much-reported problem of race relations
setter's reading: the famous recorded departure of a whole people, written up in scripture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means going out, and 'racial' refers to the Israelites as a people; the document is the second book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical book records the Israelites leaving Egypt, and the word now means any mass departure of a people.

clue.text: Threatening to accomplished players

blocks.note: something over is done, finished
the cast is the company of actors

explanation.surface: Someone menaces a group of skilled performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accomplished' looks like skilful; it means completed.
explanation.definitionFit: A clouded, gloomy sky looks threatening, as though rain is on the way.

clue.text: A liking for bird-song

blocks.note: a pen is a female swan
a chant is a simple sung melody

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of birdsong.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is the female swan; the male is a cob.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong taste or inclination for something, a fondness.

clue.text: Mass of people against the pursuit of game

blocks.note: con is the case against, as in pros and cons
to course is to hunt hares with dogs by sight

explanation.surface: A crowd protests against hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: Coursing is the field sport of chasing hares with greyhounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a large gathering or throng, a crowd coming together.

clue.text: A ne'er-do-well

blocks.note: surface reading: an idle, feckless good-for-nothing
setter's reading: one who never does well, that is, one who always does bad things

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, never doing good means doing wrong, which turns a layabout into a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicked person who commits crimes or sins is one who does no good at all.

clue.text: Keep making small change to book

blocks.note: p is a penny, the smallest coin
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps tinkering with a book in small ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small change' suggests a minor edit; it is a penny, written p.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to maintain or retain it, so keeping and preserving are synonyms.

clue.text: Airmen ready for a hot drink

blocks.note: a PO is a Pilot Officer in the RAF, so several are POs
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: Aircrew are prepared for a warming cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A posset is an old drink of hot milk curdled with ale or wine, often spiced.

clue.text: Showing nous in sorting out agreement

indicators.note: sorting out means putting into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Common sense is shown in reaching a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Nous is British slang for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in unison is to act in harmony, all together, in full concord.

clue.text: It's most economical to take meals at home

indicators.note: at means located in, so the meals are placed within the home

blocks.note: a nest is a home, especially a cosy one
to eat is to take meals

explanation.surface: Eating in is the cheapest option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Economical' suggests thrifty, but here it means tidy, with nothing wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means deft and economical of effort, so the superlative is the trimmest, least wasteful.

clue.text: There's nothing about the Man in Black being convivial

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the following word

blocks.note: O is the figure zero
c is circa, about
the Isle of Man is an island, abbreviated I
sable is black in heraldry

explanation.surface: Nothing is known about the mysterious Man in Black, yet he is friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Man in Black' looks like one person; it splits into the Isle of Man and a heraldic colour. Sable is the heraldic name for black.
explanation.definitionFit: Convivial people enjoy company and good cheer, which is what sociable means.

clue.text: Maps a sailor must return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: taken as written
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is told he must come back to his charts.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound book of maps, so the plural noun stands for it as a collection.

clue.text: Boy attending a musical presentation

blocks.note: a son is a male child
to be at an event is to attend it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy goes to a concert or show.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is an instrumental composition, here loosely called a piece presented by musicians.

clue.text: Discerning a variety of accent

blocks.note: first meaning: sharp, perceptive
second meaning: the rising mark written over a vowel, as in café

explanation.surface: Someone has an ear finely tuned to different ways of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accent' suggests regional speech; here it is a written mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, perceptive minds are sharp ones, and the e in café carries the mark of that name.

clue.text: Turn the page in error

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong or error
p is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Someone turns over the page by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn the page' looks like one action; the definition is Turn alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to rotate or twirl, which is to revolve around.

clue.text: Stand in comfort with driver

blocks.note: ease is comfort, freedom from strain
L is a learner driver, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: Someone stands comfortably beside a chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays a red L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a wooden frame that holds up a painter's canvas, a kind of support.

clue.text: Work quietly or strain as appropriate

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
p is piano, softly, in music
taken as written
a strain is a melody

explanation.surface: Advice to labour silently or exert yourself as suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like effort but is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opportune comes at a suitable or well-timed moment, which is fitting.

clue.text: Collecting rents, get mean maybe, causing antagonism

indicators.note: collecting gathers the following words into one heap for mixing together
maybe says the words are one possible arrangement, so a different order is wanted

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A greedy landlord collecting rents breeds ill will.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is the hostility or alienation that grows between people who were once close.
